tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Strong maximum principle] ↗ lem:hopfs-lemma 1. ch6:6.4-thm-3\group Maximum Principles

Assume $u \in C^2(U) \cap C(\bar U)$ and \[ c \equiv 0 \quad \text{in } U. \] Suppose also $U$ is connected, open and bounded.

(i) If \[ Lu \leq 0 \quad \text{in } U \] and $u$ attains its maximum over $\bar U$ at an interior point, then \[ u \text{ is constant within } U. \]

(ii) Similarly, if \[ Lu \geq 0 \quad \text{in } U \] and $u$ attains its minimum over $\bar U$ at an interior point, then \[ u \text{ is constant within } U. \]

Proof

\sketch If a nonconstant subsolution attained its maximum inside, take a largest ball in the strict sublevel set tangent to the maximum set. Hopf lemma gives a nonzero normal derivative at the tangency point, contradicting vanishing of the gradient at an interior maximum.

□
